title: Niger Junta Says It Contained Army Mutiny at Niamey's Base 101 After Overnight Gunfire, Explosions Near Airport and Presidency
detail: A group of soldiers rebelled against their commanding officers at Base 101 — the military installation inside Niamey's Diori Hamani International Airport that also hosts Russia's Africa Corps contingent — shortly after midnight local time on August 29, 2026, detaining fellow troops before opening fire on the airport, the perimeter of the presidential palace, and the state broadcaster's headquarters. Sustained gunfire and explosions continued for hours, briefly knocking state TV and radio off air; early wire reports citing security sources described the attackers only as 'terrorists' before Niger's Defence Ministry, in a statement read on state television and signed by Gen. Salifou Mody, clarified that 'a group of soldiers acting in breach of military regulations attempted to detain some of their comrades' — the first known internal mutiny against Gen. Abdourahamane Tchiani's junta since it seized power in the July 2023 coup. By mid-morning the ministry said security forces had fully recaptured all targeted sites and the mutiny had failed, with some participants 'neutralised' and others detained or fled; no official casualty toll was released, though online footage showed wounded individuals. AES Consultative Council member Bana Wagana Ibrahim called it 'another cowardly attack on Base 101.'
